sections.h2: Which Tennessee court handles an estate?
sections.html:
The court that exercises probate jurisdiction in the county where the person lived at death handles the estate. Tennessee statutes call this simply the court, and they define it by the decedent's legal residence on the date of death. The clerk of that county's court is the first call.

The first practical question for a family holding an inherited house is whether anyone has been appointed to act for the estate. Letters from that court show who is authorized to act for the estate, and limited letters name only the property listed in the petition. A buyer or title company may ask what authority you hold before closing.

sections.h2: What is a small estate in Tennessee?
sections.html:
A small estate is a probate estate whose property does not exceed $50,000. The Small Estate Probate Act, Tennessee Code Title 30, Chapter 4, lets one or more competent adult heirs ask for limited letters instead of opening a full administration. The 2023 rewrite of the act passed the House 90 to 0 on March 16, 2023.

  • Waiting period: a petition can be filed after 45 days from the date of death, shown by the death certificate, if no one has filed a petition to appoint a personal representative in that time. The court can waive the wait for good cause.
  • Petition: a sworn petition lists each item of property, its value, each creditor and the amount owed.
  • Bond: a corporate surety bond equal to the property value is required, unless the petitioners are the sole heirs or sole beneficiaries, or all adult heirs and beneficiaries consent in writing.
  • Creditors: no notice to creditors is published, and creditors may not file claims in the small estate.
  • Closing: the limited letters stay open until the first anniversary of issuance, when the court automatically discharges the personal representative and surety.

A will can be used too. If the decedent left a will that distributes differently than intestacy would, the named personal representative may file it as a muniment of title, or record the original with the clerk along with witness affidavits, or two disinterested persons' affidavits for a handwritten will.

sections.h2: Can a small estate petition cover the house?
sections.html:
It cannot. The act defines property as personal property only, and the model limited letters state that no real property is at issue and that the letters give the personal representative no authority over real estate. A house or land therefore needs a different route.

If extra assets turn up that push the estate over $50,000, the court may allow the small estate to be converted to a full probate administration on a verified petition filed by the personal representative or a creditor. The people who received property earlier remain liable for what they were paid.

For an heir who wants to sell the home, the clerk of the probate court is the right place to ask what documents show authority over the deed. Bring the death certificate, any will, and a list of everyone who may have an interest in the property.

sections.h2: What can the holder of small estate letters do with the property?
sections.html:
The personal representative collects and preserves the assets listed in the petition, removes personal property from a unit the decedent leased, and cancels insurance that no longer applies after the death. Anyone who owes the estate money, or holds estate property such as a bank, must pay or deliver it once shown a clerk-certified copy of the limited letters and receiving a demand. A person who hands property over in good faith is released from further liability to the estate and its creditors.

If a holder refuses, the property can be recovered, and a court can compel delivery, with costs charged to the person who wrongfully refused. Distribution then goes to the heirs as the law provides, or under the will if it was admitted as a muniment of title or recorded with the clerk. Those limits are worth knowing before an heir spends money on the house, because small estate letters reach vehicles, accounts and similar personal property, while the deed stays outside them.

sections.h2: What does full administration of an estate involve?
sections.html:
Full administration starts with letters testamentary if there is a will, or letters of administration if there is none. The steps below come from the General Assembly's bill summary of present law.

  • Inventory: within 60 days after taking office, the personal representative must complete an accurate inventory of the probate estate and return it to the clerk, verified under oath.
  • Beneficiary notice: within the same 60 days, each legatee or devisee gets a copy of the will or the relevant paragraphs, and each residuary distributee of an intestate estate gets a copy of the letters of administration.
  • Notice to creditors: within 30 days after letters are issued, the clerk publishes two consecutive weekly notices in a county newspaper, or posts written notices in three public places if the county has no newspaper.
  • Claims: creditors must file by the earlier of the dates in the notice, which includes 12 months from the date of death, or their claims are forever barred.
  • Exceptions: until 30 days after four months from the notice, the personal representative or an interested party may except to a claim in writing.

Those periods mean a house can sit in an estate for most of a year. Ask the clerk which dates apply to your file, because the notice sets them. A seller who wants speed has to work within them rather than around them.

sections.h2: How do small estate and full administration compare?
sections.html:
The comparison below shows what changes when a probate estate is under $50,000 and contains no real property. If the estate holds a house, the right column is the one that applies.

Small estate procedure and full administration in Tennessee. Sources: 2023 small estate bill text and the General Assembly's summary of present law on notice and inventory.
FeatureSmall estateFull administration
Value limit$50,000 or lessNo limit
Real propertyNot coveredNot limited to personal property
Wait to file45 days after death, unless the court waives itTiming follows the appointment and the notice dates
Notice to creditorsNone publishedTwo weekly notices in a county newspaper
Claims barCreditors may not fileEarlier of the notice dates or 12 months from death
Court involvementLimited letters, open about one yearInventory and notices to the clerk

sections.h2: What debts can follow an inherited house?
sections.html:
Medical assistance is one debt that can reach beyond the estate. The small estate statute says that if property is distributed before all medical assistance owed to TennCare under Tennessee Code section 71-5-116 is paid, both the personal representative and the person receiving the property stay liable to TennCare, up to the value received. Anyone who plans to sell inherited property should ask the clerk or an attorney whether a TennCare claim exists before sharing proceeds.

Other debts matter too. Those who receive property from a small estate remain liable for up to one year after receiving it to unpaid creditors, to anyone with a prior right to the property, and to any personal representative appointed later.

Property taxes continue while a house waits in probate. Our Tennessee property tax guide explains the bill, the appeal calendar and the relief programs, and the county trustee can give a current balance for the parcel.

faqs.q: How long does probate take in Tennessee?
faqs.a: The creditor claim period can run as long as 12 months from the date of death, which sets the pace of a full administration. A small estate stays open until the first anniversary of the limited letters. Ask the probate clerk for the dates in your own notice.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house through the small estate procedure?
faqs.a: No. The small estate law covers personal property only, and the limited letters say they give no authority over real estate. A house needs another form of probate, so ask the clerk of the court in the county where the owner lived.

faqs.q: How soon can I file a small estate petition?
faqs.a: After 45 days from the date of death, as shown by a death certificate, unless someone has already filed to appoint a personal representative. The court may waive the 45 day wait for good cause shown.

faqs.q: Do creditors get notice in a small estate?
faqs.a: No. The statute says a notice to creditors must not be published and creditors are not permitted to file claims. Recipients of property still owe unpaid creditors for up to one year after receiving it.

faqs.q: What must a personal representative do within 60 days?
faqs.a: Complete and verify an inventory of the probate estate and return it to the clerk, and send beneficiaries a copy of the will or letters. The 60 days run from entering on the administration.
